item.title: UN Urges Zambia to Halt Arbitrary Arrests of Opposition Members
item.description: The United Nations voiced concern at reports of Zambian opposition members being detained during its Aug. 13 election, while observers raised questions about the fairness of the ballot that comfortably returned President Hakainde Hichilema to power.

item.title: Kazakh Sovereign Wealth Fund to Ramp Up International Bond Sales
item.description: Kazakhstan’s sovereign wealth fund is sounding out investors as it prepares to step up international bond sales, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Canadian Stocks Climb as Trump Pauses Tariffs, Signals Deal Near
item.description: Canadian equities jumped in early trading Wednesday after US President Donald Trump said he would delay new 50% tariffs for three days and added that that two sides were close to a trade deal.

item.title: Young Americans Become More Hostile to AI, Fearing Job Losses
item.description: The youngest members of the US workforce are increasingly skeptical about artificial intelligence, fearful that advances in the technology will lead to widespread job losses, according to a Pew Research Center survey.

item.title: Dollar Tumbles as Treasury Buyback Unleashes Bond-Market Rally
item.description: The dollar tumbled by the most in three weeks to its weakest level since mid-May after the bond market rallied on the US Treasury Department’s unexpected announcement that it is increasing buybacks of long-dated bonds.

item.title: Brazilians Pour Into Chile as Winter Deluges Reopen Ski Resorts
item.description: Chile received a record number of Brazilian tourists last month as ski resorts reopened, a silver lining to the deluge of rain and heavy snows that have battered the Latin America country for weeks, and a shot in the arm to a struggling tourism industry and economy.

item.title: RBI Panel Watches Inflation as One Member Eyes Hike This Year
item.description: India’s policymakers opted to wait for more clarity on inflation before changing interest rates even as one of them saw a case for a hike later in the year, minutes of the central bank’s Aug. 3-5 meeting showed Wednesday.

item.title: Marvell Gives Google Right to Buy Up to $12 Billion in Stock
item.description: Marvell Technology Inc. and Alphabet Inc.’s Google announced an expanded chip-development partnership, including a warrant from Marvell allowing the search giant to buy as much as $12.2 billion in shares.

item.title: Long-Dated Treasuries Rally as Treasury Boosts Bond Buybacks
item.description: The US government’s longest-dated bonds rallied sharply after the Treasury Department announced it would at least double the size of buybacks in the sector.

item.title: China Criticizes EU Over Extraterritorial Reach in JD.com Probe
item.description: China criticized the European Union’s use of its Foreign Subsidies Regulation to probe JD.com Inc.’s planned €2.2 billion takeover of German electronics retailer Ceconomy, calling it an “improper extraterritorial jurisdiction” and prohibiting compliance with the measures.

item.title: India Startup Aims to Compete With OpenAI in Crowded Voice Arena
item.description: A Bangalore-based startup has entered the crowded race to build artificial voices that sound human, with an AI model that garners high scores versus systems from OpenAI and ElevenLabs Inc.

item.title: PlayStation Reboots ‘Horizon Hunters Gathering’ as Live-Service Strategy Struggles
item.description: The Japanese gaming titan has canceled or rebooted most of its live-service multiplayer projects in recent years

item.title: Anthropic-Tied Data Center Inks $1.3 Billion Private Credit Loan
item.description: Eagle Point Credit Management LLC is providing a roughly $1.3 billion private credit loan for a sprawling AI data center in Texas tied to Anthropic PBC, giving the investment firm a key role in one of the latest jumbo financings fueling the artificial intelligence boom.

item.title: Fei-Fei Li Warns US Tech Backlash Poses Risks for Global AI Progress
item.description: Fei-Fei Li, an AI pioneer, says technologists like herself need to do a better job of communicating the benefits of artificial intelligence and warns that growing public opposition in the US could carry risks for the world.

item.title: AI Cloud Firm Nebius Offers $4.5 Billion of Convertible Bonds
item.description: Nebius Group NV is tapping the convertible bond market to raise $4.5 billion, as it builds out data centers to meet the demand from artificial intelligence.

item.title: Europe Girds for Another Hike in Energy Bills This Winter
item.description: Natural gas prices are twice year-ago levels with the Iran war still in limbo.

item.title: Record Pace of Bond Sales Jolts Europe Out of Its Summer Lull
item.description: Bond sales in Europe are roaring back from the summer lull at the fastest pace on record, resuming the breakneck pace of borrowing seen globally throughout the year.

item.title: Nvidia Tries to Spur the AI Boom Into the Future
item.description: The company seeks to extend demand for the technology to a time chips will be plentiful

item.title: Ofensiva de Colombia contra la cocaína revive temores de guerra
item.description: Un nuevo presidente de línea dura apuesta por una ofensiva para combatir a los grupos armados del país.

item.title: Amazon’s New Order Confirmation Emails Seen Boosting Phishing Risk
item.description: When Dan Landau ordered a portable photo printer from Amazon.com Inc., he expected the confirmation email to tell him what was on its way. Instead, he was notified that his “luggage” was coming. In another instance, the 38-year-old head of marketing for a venture capital firm ordered items to maintain his pool and was confused when the company labeled them three different ways: “Decor,” “Outdoors” and “Garden.”

item.title: Colombia’s Former Militants Wait to See if De la Espriella Honors Petro Deal
item.description: A hawkish new president is betting big on a plan to attack the country’s armed groups

item.title: US Housing Is a Buyer’s Market. Trouble Is, There Aren’t Many Buyers
item.description: Home sales and residential construction figures are sliding as homebuyers disappear.

item.title: EQT Takes Majority Stake in Melbourne Storm Rugby League Club
item.description: Swedish buyout firm EQT AB has moved into a niche corner of the global sports market by taking a majority stake in Melbourne Storm, one of Australia’s leading rugby league clubs.

item.title: Saudis Give Full Oil Allocations to at Least Three Europe Buyers
item.description: Saudi Aramco has notified at least three European oil refiners that will supply full contractual crude volumes next month, easing concerns about the region’s supply concerns while crude flows from the Persian Gulf and Red Sea are disrupted.

item.title: AI Data Center Political Opposition to Bring Stock Market Winners and Losers
item.description: Data center opposition will be a drag on performance

item.title: Lowe’s Cuts Outlook as Soft Housing Market Curbs Demand
item.description: Lowe’s Cos. cut its outlook for the full year after posting results that missed Wall Street estimates, showing how a stubbornly weak housing market is eroding the home-improvement retailer’s performance.

item.title: Sweden Is Set to Keep 2026 Rate Hike on Table: Decision Guide
item.description: Sweden’s Riksbank is set to restate its readiness to raise interest rates this year if the Iran war leads to a spike in inflation in the largest Nordic economy.

item.title: Deutsche Bank’s Uleer Says Stocks Can Power Through Rate Rise
item.description: Equities face no serious threat from higher bond yields or oil prices as long as Brent crude stays below $100 a barrel, according to Maximilian Uleer of Deutsche Bank AG.

item.title: Shorter Is Better to Bond Traders Seeking Shelter
item.description: The hot safety play is a short-dated bond.

item.title: UK House Prices Post First Fall This Year, Official Data Show
item.description: UK house prices fell for the first time this year, according to official data that showed a property market malaise spreading after the Iran war pushed up mortgage costs.
